episode_title: Managing the Momentum in Risk Management with Lawanda "Elle Michell" Hall

real_qa.q: What is the definition of risk management according to industry experts?
real_qa.r: Lawanda Hall defines risk management as managing the momentum of the moment—understanding what an organization is doing or not doing today and how that will impact the future state. Risk managers take data and information to determine how current behaviors, operations, and manufacturing practices will affect future outcomes. The discipline involves looking at data to understand what is probable and using various risk tools to ensure the risk strategy aligns with the organization's business objectives and risk appetite.

real_qa.q: Why is Southern University the only HBCU with a risk management and insurance major?
real_qa.r: Southern University's dean of business Dr. Andrews and chancellor Jean-Pierre recognized that the insurance industry has significant talent gaps due to Baby Boomer retirums and a lack of generational pipeline. In partnership with the Alliant Insurance Foundation, they created a comprehensive risk management and insurance major program that includes not only academics but also scholarships, internships, and mentorship opportunities—critical support for first-generation college and first-generation risk management students.
real_qa.requete: Southern University risk management major HBCU

real_qa.q: How does the Spencer Education Foundation support risk management education at HBCUs?
real_qa.r: Lawanda Hall works through the Spencer Education Foundation to help stand up and expand risk management programs serving Black and Brown students. The foundation's support enables institutions to create structured pathways into the GRC field for students who historically had no visibility into risk management as a career option, even in households with corporate professionals.
real_qa.requete: Spencer Education Foundation risk management programs HBCUs

real_qa.q: What role does coaching play in developing new talent in governance risk and compliance?
real_qa.r: Hall emphasizes that organizations should provide internal coaching for young GRC professionals in addition to education, as coaching helps elevate professionals and amplifies their learning. Coaching accelerates professional maturity, helps professionals understand the culture and subculture of GRC, and provides the courage and confidence required to navigate the space effectively. Given the mass exodus of experienced talent, coaching young professionals helps them ramp up into leadership roles faster than previous generations.
real_qa.requete: coaching young professionals GRC risk management

real_qa.q: Why does risk management apply to all industries including unexpected sectors like repossession?
real_qa.r: Risk management is a niche discipline but applies across all industries because every industry has some form of regulation, governance, compliance requirements, risk exposure, and insurance needs. Monica Reger provides the example of a compliance manager working in repossession who manages risk around vehicle liability and insurance coverage—illustrating that wherever there is business activity, industry-specific risk management principles apply.
